prompt: Stage 4-1, level 6, 58 gold, 61 HP, three losses in a row. You are 14 XP from level 7. Your carry is a 1-star 3-cost with two items and your tank is a 2-star 2-cost; the rest of the board is 2-star 1- and 2-costs. This is the round the plan has been saving for. What do you do?

options.label: Buy level 7 (14 gold), then roll down to about 20 gold looking for the 2-star on your carry and a stronger seventh unit
Stay level 6 and keep the 58: 5 interest a round is too good to give up
Roll all 58 at level 6 without levelling; 3-costs are 25% at level 6 and you need the carry copies

explanation:
4-1 is the round the plan saves for: level 7, then roll. At level 7 the shop shows 3-costs 43% of the time per slot (25% at level 6) and 4-costs at 10% instead of 5%, so every 2 gold you roll after levelling is worth almost twice as much for the carry you need. Level first, because it also adds a seventh unit to a board that is losing. 58 minus 14 leaves 44; rolling to about 20 keeps 2 interest and gives you twelve refreshes at the better odds. Stop when the carry is 2-star or when you reach the gold you promised to keep.

Holding at 61 HP on three losses means stage-4 losses of 10 or more HP each while you earn 5 interest: the maths does not work. Rolling at level 6 without levelling spends the same gold at half the odds and leaves you a unit short for the whole of stage 4. Level, then roll; not the other way round and not neither.
principle: At 4-1: level to 7 first, then roll for the upgrades. The bank was for this.
commonMistake: Rolling at 4-1 before buying level 7, or sitting on 50 gold at 60 HP because interest feels safer than spending.
hint: Compare the 3-cost and 4-cost odds at level 6 and level 7, and count the HP three more stage-4 losses would cost.
